issues.spec_reference: spec.tex line 2182: "The original model is not changed; a failed completion does not stop the solve."
issues.location: src/fleet_management/degradation_model/base.py, complete_binary_warm_start, lines 488 (fixed.optimize()) and 506 (fixed.computeIIS()); no try/except in the function or in solve_mixed (lines 1350-1353)
issues.description: The code treats a completion that ends without a solution (status infeasible, time_limit, other) as a failed completion and the solve goes on. It does not catch an exception. A GurobiError from the optimisation of the copy or from computeIIS (for example an IIS request that Gurobi refuses for a model with indicator or nonconvex quadratic rows, or a licence or memory error in the copy) leaves complete_binary_warm_start, so solve()/solve_mapping() raises, and in a sweep the case becomes an error row. The spec sentence says that a failed completion never stops the solve. The same exception path exists for the relaxation start (lines 546-553), where the spec says nothing. The tests probably do not reach it, because they only use statuses.
issues.suggested_fix: Either wrap the copy, the optimisation and computeIIS in try/except Exception, record the status as "status_error" (or similar) and continue, and add this status to the spec table of completion; or restrict the spec sentence to "a completion that ends without a solution does not stop the solve".

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 1932-1946 (arguments of sweep_operating_horizons): objective_mode default "operating_average"; "\"evaluation_total\" needs E > H_1"; lines 2014 and 2087 (objective is a text; modes "evaluation_total" and "operating_average")
issues.location: src/fleet_management/horizon_sweep.py lines 93-100 (SWEEP_OBJECTIVES has the key "total") and line 632 (objective_mode not in OBJECTIVE_MODES); config.py line 45 (OBJECTIVE_MODES = ("total", "operating_average", "evaluation_total"))
issues.description: sweep_operating_horizons accepts objective_mode="total" and writes it into every case input. The report then holds the objective text "minimize J_initialization + J_op + C_D*u; rank by J_op/H2". The spec table gives no list of valid values for the argument of the sweep, names only two modes, and does not describe this third mode, its objective text, or the fact that the ranking still uses J_op/H2. issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 2092-2095 (errors of sweep_horizon_grid: only ValueError for evaluation_horizon) and lines 2074-2083 (argument rules)
issues.location: src/fleet_management/horizon_sweep.py sweep_horizon_grid lines 873-904: _positive_integers (lines 123-131, lines 127 and 130), line 877-880 (objective_mode in sweep_options raises ValueError), line 902 (_check_sweep_arguments for every H1, with all its ValueErrors; an unknown option is a Python TypeError), line 904 (_check_output_path)
issues.description: The grid raises more errors than the one in its error table: an empty list or a non-positive or non-integer entry in transitory_horizons or operating_horizons (ValueError), objective_mode inside the keyword options (ValueError, although the spec says only that the options are those of sweep_operating_horizons except objective_mode), every invalid sweep option such as gradient_tolerance or minimum_cases, an output_path whose extension is not .yaml or .yml, and an unknown option name (TypeError). issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 1991-2002 (stop rule: "The last candidate of operating_horizons is a hard limit") and line 2021 (stopping_rule.reason: "in_progress", "candidate_range_exhausted", "cost_increase" or "flat_gradient"; stopped_early = complete with fewer cases than planned)
issues.description: The stop rule is tested after every case, also after the last candidate. If the rule holds after the last candidate, the final report has reason "cost_increase" or "flat_gradient" with stopped_early false (no case is skipped). The spec does not say which reason a sweep reports when the rule fires on the last candidate, and the sentence on the hard limit can be read as "candidate_range_exhausted". Tests that stop in the middle of the list do not show it.
issues.suggested_fix: State in the spec: "If the rule holds after the last candidate, reason is the reason of the rule and stopped_early is false" (this is what the code does), or change the code to report "candidate_range_exhausted" when no candidate is left.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex line 2049: "F, M, L are read from the input data, null if they cannot be read" and line 2016 (fixed_dimensions: F, M, L)
issues.description: The code returns F, M and L all null as soon as one of them cannot be read (for example F and M are valid but L cannot be inferred from model). The spec sentence can be read entry by entry. The same all-or-nothing dictionary is used in fixed_dimensions of the report and in the dimensions of every error row. L is inferred from model and the optional key L, which the spec sentence does not mention.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 1933 and 1950-1952 (H_1 is the first entry of H, or H; steps 1 and 2: read the file, check every argument)
issues.location: src/fleet_management/horizon_sweep.py _horizon_H1 lines 134-141 and call at line 826, before _check_sweep_arguments (line 827)
issues.description: H_1 is read from the data before any argument is checked. A missing H, an H that is not an integer (ValueError from _integer, line 141) or H_1 with any integer value (zero or negative is accepted by _integer, no positivity check) are not covered. A missing or invalid H raises ValueError before the argument checks, in an order the spec does not state (spec step 2 comes after step 1 and lists only the list of wrong length). H_1 <= 0 is not rejected here; each case then fails as a case error and the sweep returns a report of error rows.
issues.suggested_fix: Add to the error table: ValueError when H is missing or is not an integer or a pair of integers, raised before the argument checks; and decide whether H_1 < 1 is a ValueError (code change) or a case error (document it).

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 2184-2199 (relaxation start: "relax its linear rows with Gurobi's feasRelaxS (sum of absolute violations); integrality, variable bounds and general constraints are kept") and line 1866 (relaxation_objective: objective value of the relaxed copy)
issues.location: src/fleet_management/degradation_model/base.py apply_relaxation_warm_start lines 546-570, call at line 552: relaxed.feasRelaxS(0, False, False, True)
issues.description: The call uses minrelax=False. By the Gurobi documentation, the relaxed copy then minimises only the cost of the violation, so the original objective is dropped, and relaxation_objective is the total violation, not an objective of the fleet problem (with minrelax=True the original objective would be kept among the minimum-violation solutions). The spec does not say that the objective is replaced. Gurobi relaxes bounds and linear constraints only; the spec does not say that the quadratic rows of the exact form are kept unrelaxed (it names only integrality, bounds and general constraints). Also, the relaxed copy is optimised with the options of the original model: the spec does not say whether it writes to the log or to the log file of the solve (the completion copy sets OutputFlag, LogToConsole and LogFile off, lines 483-485; the relaxation copy does not). The status string is the output of status_string ("optimal", "time_limit", ..., "gurobi_status_<q>"), a set that the spec does not list; the completion uses a different spelling ("status_<q>").
issues.suggested_fix: Add to the section Relaxation Start: the objective of the copy is the sum of absolute violations only (the original objective is not used); quadratic rows are not relaxed; the relaxed copy is silent (or not); the list of status strings of the relaxation (the strings of status_string, with "gurobi_status_<q>" for another code).

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 1850-1856 (completion keys: fixed_integer_variables, values_copied, runtime_seconds) and lines 2178-2180 (steps: fix every binary variable that has a Start value; optimise the copy)
issues.description: (a) When the completion does not run, fixed_integer_variables is 0, values_copied is 0, runtime_seconds is null and iis_constraints is []; the spec gives the status only. (b) runtime_seconds is the Gurobi Runtime attribute of the optimisation of the copy; it excludes the copy, the fixing and the IIS, while the spec says "runtime of the completion". (c) The code fixes every variable of type BINARY or INTEGER that has a Start value, the spec step says binary variables (the report key says integer variables). (d) completion_time_limit of the source is used as given, with no check (a negative, null or non-numeric value raises in float() or in Gurobi).
issues.suggested_fix: State the values of the keys when the completion does not run; define runtime_seconds as the Gurobi runtime of the optimisation of the copy; say "binary or integer variable" in step 1; state the rule for completion_time_limit (a number >= 0).

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex line 2153: "The mapped values, rounded to the nearest integer"
issues.description: Python round() on a float rounds a tie to the even integer (0.5 gives 0, 1.5 gives 2). The spec says "nearest integer" without a tie rule. For a source whose entries are 0 or 1 the difference never shows. A value above 1 or below 0 in a hand-made source is also passed to a binary variable as Start or VarHintVal without any check or clipping, which the spec does not state.
issues.suggested_fix: Add "a tie goes to the even integer" (the Python rule), and state that the rounded value is not clipped to [0, 1]; or clip and document it.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 2056-2060 (parallel cases: "each in its own process with its own Gurobi environment and one Gurobi licence token")
issues.location: src/fleet_management/horizon_sweep.py _sweep lines 762-783 (ProcessPoolExecutor with the spawn start method)
issues.description: The cases run in a pool of n_workers processes, created with the "spawn" start method. A worker process solves several cases one after another when there are more cases than workers, so a case does not have a process of its own. If a worker dies, the pool is broken and every case not yet finished gets an error row (the same error message). The spec states neither the start method nor the broken-pool behaviour. The number of licence tokens is the number of worker processes, not the number of cases.
issues.suggested_fix: Write: "up to n_workers worker processes (start method spawn) take the cases in turn; a worker solves one case at a time with its own Gurobi environment; if a worker process dies, all unfinished cases are recorded as case errors".

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 2205-2207 and 1905-1914 (a source is the result of the nearest preceding case with a solution; a feasible case is one whose result holds a solution)
issues.location: src/fleet_management/horizon_sweep.py _source_of line 225 (x is not None) and _is_feasible line 254 (row objective is not None); _case_row line 207 and config _to_plain lines 191-192
issues.description: The two notions of "has a solution" use different tests: a warm-start source needs the array x, a feasible case needs a non-null objective in the row. The row passes through _to_plain, which turns a NaN or infinite value into null. A result that has a solution but an objective that is NaN or infinite (or a status that does not allow it) would be a source but not feasible, and a row with a null objective is never ranked. The spec uses one phrase for both. In addition the spec says the gradient is available if both cases are feasible, and the case after such a row is annotated "unavailable". This is a rare branch, the tests have no case for it.
issues.suggested_fix: Define "has a solution" once in the spec as the test the code uses for each purpose (source: the result has x; feasible: the row has an objective that is not null and a status outside the three), or make the code use one test.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 1968-1989 (early stop: eligibility "if cases n-1 and n qualify"; annotation of every row)
issues.description: The code sets gradient_stopping_eligible to true only if the gradient is available, that is, both cases are feasible; for a row without an available gradient it is false even if cases n-1 and n both report a finite gap. The spec defines eligibility by qualification alone, with no mention of feasibility. A case that is not feasible has no gap in practice, so the difference is invisible, but the spec text and the code differ in definition.
issues.suggested_fix: In the definition of "Eligible to stop" add "and the gradient of case n is available".
